summary: Two measured one-line fixes handed over by W1-30B and W1-30F, each falling in the other's file. Both were real, and neither was the whole story. Fix 1 (province.js caster flags) is landed for terrain, geology and canopy — the canopy only after a 1080p hardware budget OVERTURNED my own written ruling against it. Fix 2 (renderer.js height_falloff_m) is landed but was decorative on its own: sky.js's stand-in table holds the same thirteen numbers. Pulling that thread found a third defect underneath it that neither child could have seen from inside its own file: game/src/world/aerial.js and game/src/render/sky.js each patch the SAME four THREE.ShaderChunk fog chunks at module scope, aerial.js runs second, and it had been silently deleting sky.js's whole atmosphere model since the day both landed. That is fixed, and fixing it is what makes fix 2 mean anything.
headline_findings: F1 — THE FOG SHADERCHUNK COLLISION, THE BIGGEST THING HERE, AND IT WAS NOT IN THE BRIEF. Read out of the running page, not inferred: `THREE.ShaderChunk.fog_fragment` was carrying `esAerialScale`, i.e. `world/aerial.js`'s strings, not `render/sky.js`'s. Both patch the same four chunks at module scope; `renderer.js` imports `./sky.js` (line 18) before `../world/province.js` (line 19), and province.js installed at module scope, so it won last. `sky.js` sets `scene.fog` to `HeightFog extends THREE.Fog` and REPURPOSES `fogNear` as sigma0 (~0.0068/m) and `fogFar` as H (26-340 m) — a repurposing only its own chunks understand. aerial.js's chunk read the stock meaning off those two floats: `smoothstep(fogNear, fogFar, depth*esAerial)` = `smoothstep(0.0068, 55, depth*0.76)` at the Blackwood vista camera. TOTAL FOG AT ABOUT 72 METRES. The province beyond roughly one tile was a flat wash of fog colour and W1-30B's measured '35% of contrast survives at 150 m' was not running at all. Neither piece's controls could catch it — each arm flips its own switch and both switches still appear to work. After the fix the same probe says the chunks are owned by `render/sky.js`, and the hardware Deck's Salt Hills vista now reads a settlement several hundred metres away against a horizon.

F2 — THE 1080p HARDWARE BUDGET OVERTURNED MY OWN RULING, AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL NUMBER IN THIS FILE. I had written R4 declining the canopy on cost, priced in triangles, with 'what would overturn it: a 1080p hardware frame-time budget'. I then took that budget — NVIDIA L4, ANGLE/Vulkan 1.4.312, 1920x1080, pixel ratio pinned, 60 frames per arm — and it says the cost is not there. Salt Hills: base 13.73 ms median at 485,458 shadow-pass triangles, everything-on 13.98 ms at 1,829,748. Spawn: 14.37 -> 14.30. Blackwood: 6.09 -> 6.01. The arms are not even MONOTONE in triangle count (terrain+canopy+geology is 13.28 ms at Salt Hills, faster than base), which is what 'below the noise' looks like. `province.js`'s own comment claiming 18 ms on a T4 for the scatter does not reproduce against the current 150 m / 4096 fit. So the canopy landed.

F3 — WHAT EACH SUBSET ACTUALLY BUYS, measured as the shadow sabotage on the same frame. At the Blackwood region vista: terrain alone 0.009%, +canopy 17.72%, +geology 17.68%, +understorey and scatter-rock 17.61%, +ground cover 17.94%, and W1-30B's flip-everything ceiling was 18.3%. THE CANOPY IS THE ENTIRE EFFECT AT THAT CAMERA. `under`, `rock` and `cover` are 476,000 more triangles for about 0.2 points between them and are NOT landed.

F4 — THE COST, EXACTLY, off the scene graph over the 5x5 resident set. The shadow atlas already carried 361,838 triangles across 1,258 casters before any of this. `ground` is 96,800 (TILE_SEG 44, 3,872/tile, 25 tiles) and `ground-skin` is 30,752, so the terrain is +35.3%. `geology` is 3,600 in Blackwood and 6,120 in the Salt Hills — the cheapest thing in the province and the population a missing contact shadow is most obvious under. The canopy is 605,072 (tile scatter) + 258,104 (near disc) = 863,176 in Blackwood, 219,648 in the Salt Hills.

F5 — THE STRIPES WERE NOT MINE, AND I NEARLY REPORTED THAT THEY WERE. The hardware Deep Marshes vista shows regular parallel bands across the ground — 7.57% row-to-row luminance jumps in the lower half against 0.90% in the Salt Hills — and the honest first reading was 'that is terrain shadow acne and I put it there'. The A/B says otherwise: put `ground.castShadow` and `ground-skin.castShadow` back to false in the page and the bands are IDENTICAL. They belong to something that was already casting (the province is full of posts, piles and landmark trunks that always have). The whole difference between terrain-casting and not, at that camera, is 1.394% of pixels and none of it is striped. `tools/visual/w1-30-terrain-acne-ab.mjs`.

F6 — FIX 2 AS BRIEFED MOVES NO PIXEL, AND THE REASON MATTERS. `sky.js`'s `REGION_HEIGHT_FALLOFF_M` is keyed on each region's fog colour and its thirteen values are IDENTICAL to `regions.json`'s thirteen `fog.height_falloff_m` (55/150/120/26/50/45/55/340/200/190/110/260/70). A before/after screenshot pair of the one-line change is therefore the fifth control failure in HAZARDS §0 — both arms agree, wrongly, that the table and the JSON are the same thing. What the change does is decide which of the two is AUTHORITATIVE, and that is proved by an arm that can fail (see null_controls).

F7 — AN ARM-TO-ARM IMAGE DIFF IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT AT A FOLIAGE SITE. `vista-blackwood` base vs terrain measured 77.6% of pixels changed on SwiftShader, which looks like an enormous win and is not: the frames are ~20 simulation steps apart and the frame is almost entirely animated foliage. Side by side they are the same picture. Only the WITHIN-arm sabotage diff means anything. Recorded so nobody quotes the 77%.

F9 — THE CANOPY DOES NOT SHIMMER, MEASURED IN MOTION ON HARDWARE, AND THIS CLOSES THE GAP THIS FILE ORIGINALLY DECLARED. Identical 90-frame walks at 1920x1080 on an NVIDIA L4, three arms, two regions, adjacent-frame mean absolute luminance change. eye-blackwood: A (canopy casts) 1.9119, B (canopy does not) 2.3413, C (no sun shadow at all) 2.3303. eye-deep-marshes: 1.9055 / 2.3661 / 2.3555. Two independent regions agree to within 1.3%. Flicker would push arm A UP against arm B; it is DOWN, by 18.3% and 19.5%. No shimmer. CAVEAT THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THE NUMBER: this metric is mean ABSOLUTE luminance change, shadowing darkens the ground, and a darker image has smaller absolute deltas — so the magnitude of the reduction is confounded with darkening and must not be quoted as 'the frame got 18% calmer'. The DIRECTION is what supports the negative claim, and the negative claim is the one that was owed.

F10 — B/C = 1.005 AT BOTH SITES, WHICH IS A SEPARATE FINDING AND A BLUNT ONE. With the canopy not casting, the entire sun shadow system changes frame-to-frame motion by half a percent against having no shadow at all. In other words, before this piece, walking through Blackwood or the Deep Marshes at eye level, the shadows were doing essentially NOTHING. That is the same defect W1-30B measured as 0.0-1.5% on the region vistas, now confirmed from the other direction and in motion.

F11 — MY OWN VERDICT RULE WAS ONE-SIDED AND PRINTED 'NO POWER' OVER A REAL RESULT. `w1-30-canopy-shimmer.mjs` asked `(A/C) > 1.02 || (B/C) > 1.02` — whether an arm was NOISIER than the no-shadow floor. Arm A came back at A/C = 0.82, an 18% departure from the floor in the QUIETER direction, and the tool reported that the instrument was blind. It was not; I had only given it one eye. Both hardware manifests carry that wrong string. The rule is now two-sided (`|ratio - 1| > 0.02`) and power is assessed PER ARM, because B sitting on C is a finding about B, not a broken instrument; `reports/runpod-gpu/runs/canopy-shimmer/verdict-recomputed.json` carries the corrected verdicts and says plainly that it supersedes the manifests. A guard that can only see deviation in the direction you expected is the same failure as a control that cannot fail.

F8 — `vista-blackwood` IS NOT A VISTA. 26 m above the player, -11 degrees of pitch, and no horizon and no sky anywhere in frame — only very large near geometry. Every frame this piece and W1-30B have taken there shows it. Same family as W1-30V's `vista-valus-ridge` finding (which this run's hardware frame confirms: sky over an empty plateau). It is why the terrain arm reads 0.009% there while the hardware Salt Hills frame shows terrain shadow plainly.
reversible_rulings: R1 (reversible, one line, LARGEST BLAST RADIUS, NOT IN THE BRIEF) — `installAerialPerspective()` is commented out in `game/src/world/province.js`. Reversal: uncomment it. Nothing is lost: `sky.js`'s `ES_FOG_FRAGMENT` is the same physics done better — it integrates Beer-Lambert through an exponential haze layer of scale height H between camera Y and fragment Y, where aerial.js multiplies a scale onto a smoothstep — and the thirteen numbers W1-30F went and found are not lost either, because `renderer.js` now carries `fog.height_falloff_m` to exactly that H every frame. `_updateAerial()` is deliberately LEFT RUNNING so `province.stats().aerial` keeps reporting and any instrument reading it keeps working. WHAT WOULD OVERTURN IT: a capture showing sky.js's model is the worse picture, or a consumer that needs `uAerial` bound. It is also the reversal W1-30F wrote down itself.
R2 (reversible, one flag each) — `ground.castShadow = true`, `ground-skin.castShadow = true`. +127,552 triangles. No acne (F5). WHAT WOULD OVERTURN IT: acne at a sun angle or region I did not sample.
R3 (reversible, one flag) — `geology:* castShadow = true`. +3,600 triangles in Blackwood.

R4 — WITHDRAWN BY ITS OWN TRIPWIRE, AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS THE POINT. I wrote R4 declining the canopy on cost and naming the evidence that would overturn it; I then went and got that evidence and it overturned it (F2). The canopy now casts: `im.castShadow = b.kind === 'canopy'` in both the near disc and the tile scatter. Reversal: put either line back to `false`.

R5 (reversible, NOT taken) — `under`, the scatter's `rock` bucket and `cover` do NOT cast: 476,000 triangles for about 0.2 points of the vista. `under` in particular is a grass blade, sub-texel in a 4096 map fitted to 150 m, and a sub-texel caster is the classic source of shimmer as the camera moves — which is exactly what this piece could not test (no motion capture). WHAT WOULD OVERTURN IT: a motion sequence showing they are stable, plus a reason to want them.

R6 (reversible, NOT taken, AGAINST THE BRIEF) — `province-far.receiveShadow` is left `false`. RADIUS 2 and TILE_M 300 put 750 m of detailed ground between the camera and the far mesh in every direction while the shadow distance is 150 m, so the far mesh is never inside the volume where it is visible; flipping it measured +0.044 points at the Salt Hills, which is noise, against a per-pixel shadow sample on the largest mesh in the frame. WHAT WOULD OVERTURN IT: a shadow distance above 750 m.
what_landed: game/src/render/renderer.js:1173 — `regionFog` carries `heightFalloffM: r.fog.height_falloff_m`. FIX 2 as briefed. `sky.js` already preferred that property; its colour-keyed table stays as the fallback for a colour it does not know.
game/src/world/province.js:144 — `installAerialPerspective()` commented out, with the measurement and the one-line reversal in the comment. R1.
game/src/world/province.js — `ground.castShadow`, `ground-skin.castShadow`, `geology:* castShadow`, and `castShadow = b.kind === 'canopy'` on both the near disc and the tile scatter. FIX 1.

null_controls: FIX 2 — the plausible wrong answer, not the trivial one. The trivial control is `setFeature('heightFog', false)`, which proves the MODEL is live, says nothing about where its parameter came from, and would have passed BEFORE the fix. The control that can fail: perturb the region record the renderer actually reads (western-rootlands, H 70 -> 280) and re-render. WITH the fix, `scene.fog.heightFalloff` follows 70 -> 280 and 6.471% of the frame moves. WITH THE FIX DELETED — `--deleteFix` wraps `sky.apply()` and strips the property, which is byte-for-byte the pre-fix state — `scene.fog.heightFalloff` stays at 70, the JSON is ignored and the table wins, exactly the defect, and the frame moves 2.552%, which is that site's own nondeterminism floor. Signal 6.47 against a floor of 2.55; the state readout 70->280 vs 70->70 is unambiguous.

FIX 1 — the plausible wrong answer, not the trivial one. The trivial control is 'no shadows at all' and `setFeature('shadows', false)` already is it. The plausible wrong answer a hurried fix ships is `wrongset`: casters on, receivers untouched, so trees and hills cast into a world where `province-far` still refuses and `ground` still does not. Measured: 17.587% at Blackwood for 1,748,868 triangles — it pays 3.6x the atlas for a shadow that stops at the tile seam with no landform self-shadowing behind it.

THE ACNE ACCUSATION — falsified rather than assumed. Arm B put the terrain caster flags back in the page and the Deep Marshes bands were identical. That control could have condemned the change and did not.

THE ONE I COULD NOT BUILD, stated rather than faked. 'A tree floats above its own shadow' is not reproducible in this build: `updateOcclusion()` collapses an occluding instance by scaling its matrix to 0.001 and the shadow pass reads the same instance matrix, so a hidden tree's shadow goes with it. Good property; it forced the wrongset substitution.

THE CANOPY IN MOTION — the plausible wrong answer, not the trivial one. The trivial control is a still camera: no motion, no shimmer, proves nothing. The plausible wrong answer is that the walk is so noisy on its own — wind on the leaves, water, streaming pop — that it swamps any shadow flicker and BOTH arms look identical, a test that cannot fail. So arm C walks the identical path with the sun shadow switched off entirely: that is the floor this world's own motion makes with no shadow in it. It came back at B/C = 1.005 at both sites, which means arm B genuinely has no power AND is itself the finding in F10, while arm A departs from that floor by 18-20% in the quieter direction.

could_not_do: CLOSED AFTER THE FACT — the motion gap. This file originally declared 'no motion evidence of my own' as its largest could-not-do. It has since been taken: `tools/visual/w1-30-canopy-shimmer.mjs` on a rented L4, three arms, two regions, 90-frame walks at 1080p (F9, F11). What remains genuinely untaken is the OTHER motion question — whether the fitted shadow volume's edge crawls as the camera advances now that the terrain casts. The shimmer walk would not separate that from everything else moving in frame; it needs a static-camera, moving-sun or a boundary-crossing sequence, and it has not been done.

THE 12 HARDWARE DECK MOTION SEQUENCES ARE STALE. They were captured at the state before the canopy and geology flags landed, so they show the fog fix and terrain casting only. The shimmer run covers the canopy in motion at two sites; the other ten regions have stills only.

THE SHIMMER METRIC IS NOT CONTRAST-NORMALISED. Mean absolute luminance change is confounded with overall brightness, which is why F9 reports a direction and refuses to quote the magnitude as a quality score. A contrast-normalised or ground-masked metric would quantify it properly and I did not write one.

NO LOCAL FRAME-TIME NUMBER, and I stopped trying rather than quote one. This box sat at load 13-22 on 4 cores all session, SwiftShader is CPU-bound, and one 1920x1080 frame took about 40 seconds — the arms differ by less than the noise between two consecutive frames of the SAME arm. The budget that matters was taken on rented hardware instead.

I killed two capture runs on false evidence: `| tail -40` buffers a pipeline until it exits, so runs that were progressing normally looked hung. One of those was a genuine browser crash at 1920x1080 (devicePixelRatio 2 on a 960x540 request); the tool now pins the pixel ratio. Roughly forty minutes lost to it.

The pixel arms were taken at ONE local site (vista-blackwood) and three hardware sites (blackwood, salt-hills, spawn). Ten of the thirteen region vistas have a hardware still from this run but no per-subset sabotage measurement.

`vista-blackwood`'s first hardware arm reads 98.114% shadow, which is a settling artefact of the first sabotage pair at a site and not a measurement; the `terrain` arm's 0.009% at the same camera is the real number. The tool should take a throwaway pair before the first arm and does not.
`vista-blackwood` could not be used to judge anything (F8) and I did not fix it — a camera-placement defect, not this piece's file.

I did not delete `sky.js`'s `REGION_HEIGHT_FALLOFF_M`, which its own comment asks for once `heightFalloffM` exists. It is now unreachable for all thirteen regions but is a real fallback for a fourteenth, `sky.js` is another live piece's file this round, and deleting it buys nothing measurable.
No human read and no Craft number.
notes_for_others: W1-30B and W1-30F: your two pieces collided in `THREE.ShaderChunk` and neither of you could have seen it from inside your own file. Both models are the same physics; sky.js's is the better implementation and it now runs, fed by the thirteen numbers W1-30F went and found. Nothing was thrown away.

ANYONE PATCHING `THREE.ShaderChunk`: two module-scope patches of the same chunk is a silent last-writer-wins, and the loser's feature flag still appears to work because it toggles state the shader no longer reads. A one-line probe catches it — read the chunk back out of the page and assert whose marker string is in it. This is worth a standing gate and I did not have the budget to write one.

ANYONE ABOUT TO DECLINE SOMETHING ON RENDER COST: the shadow-pass budget on this game at 1080p is not where the comments in `province.js` say it is. Going from 485k to 1.83M shadow-pass triangles is free on an L4. `tools/visual/w1-30-shadow-casters.mjs --hardware --perfFrames 60` through `tools/runpod/cli.mjs run --command` takes the measurement for about nine cents in ten minutes; do that before writing another 18-ms comment.
W1-30V: `vista-blackwood` joins `vista-valus-ridge` as a Deck stop that cannot show what it is named for.

Whoever wants distance-limited casters: the tile scatter is one InstancedMesh per bucket per REGION across the whole 5x5 resident set, so its bounding sphere is ~1.5 km and `frustumCulled` can never cull it against a 150 m shadow camera. Per-tile buckets would make it free. Given F2 there is no longer a cost reason to want it, but there may be a shimmer reason.

W1-30B's `worldCastersOn` arm (18.3% of the Blackwood vista) is the CEILING of the whole flag change, not a proposal. This piece reached 17.7% of it for 863,176 of the 1,467,910 triangles that ceiling costs.

ANYONE WRITING A POWER OR NOISE GUARD: make it two-sided. Mine asked 'is this arm noisier than the floor' and printed NO POWER over an 18% departure in the quieter direction (F11). Ask |ratio - 1|, and assess power per arm rather than per run.
next_step: A fresh critic on R1 first — largest blast radius, not in the brief, changes the atmosphere of every frame. Then the one motion question still open: does the fitted shadow volume's edge crawl now that the terrain casts? That needs a static-camera or boundary-crossing sequence, not the shimmer walk.
